Genesis 11

Beside elohim: SG singular agreement, PL plural agreement, ? checked, undetermined.

And all the earth had one language and the same devarim . As they traveled from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there. They said to one another, “Come on, let's make bricks and fire them thoroughly.” The bricks served as stone for them, and the bitumen served as mortar for them. They said, “Come on, let's build for ourselves a city and a tower, with its top in the sky, and let's make a name for ourselves, so that we won't scatter across the surface of the whole earth.” Then Yahweh came down to see the city and the tower that the children of humankind had built. And Yahweh said, “Look, they are one people and have one language for all of them, and this is what they have begun to do. And now nothing that they plan to do will be beyond reach for them. Come, let us go down and confuse their language there, so that they will not understand each his neighbor’s language.” And Yahweh scattered them from there across the surface of the whole earth, and they stopped building the city. That is why it was called Babel , because there Yahweh confused the language of the whole earth, and from there Yahweh scattered them across the surface of the whole earth. These are the descendants of Shem . Shem was a hundred years old, and he fathered Arphaxad two years after the mabul . And Shem lived after he fathered Arphaxad five hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters. And Arphaxad lived thirty-five years and fathered Shelah . And Arphaxad lived 403 years after he fathered Shelah , and he fathered sons and daughters. And Shelah lived thirty years and fathered Eber . And Shelah lived after he fathered Eber 403 years and he fathered sons and daughters. And Eber lived thirty-four years and fathered Peleg . And Eber lived after he fathered Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and he fathered sons and daughters. And Peleg lived thirty years and fathered Reu . And Peleg lived 209 years after he fathered Reu , and he fathered sons and daughters. And Reu lived thirty-two years and fathered Serug . And Reu lived 207 years after he fathered Serug , and he fathered sons and daughters. And Serug lived 30 years and fathered Nahor . And Serug lived two hundred years after he fathered Nahor , and he fathered sons and daughters. And Nahor lived 29 years and fathered Terah . And Nahor lived 119 years after he fathered Terah , and he fathered sons and daughters. And Terah lived seventy years, and he fathered Abram , Nahor and Haran . And these are the descendants of Terah : Terah fathered Abram , Nahor and Haran , and Haran fathered Lot . And Haran died in the presence of Terah his father, in the land of his birth, in Ur of Chaldeans . And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. The name of the wife of Abram was Sarai , and the name of the wife of Nahor was Milcah , the daughter of Haran , the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah . And Sarai was unable to bear children; she had no child. Then Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran , his son's son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of Abram his son. And they went out with them from Ur of Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan . They came as far as Haran and settled there. The days of Terah were two hundred and five years, and Terah died in Haran .

Manuscript differences

There is no Kainan here: Genesis follows the Hebrew genealogy.

Septuagint

The Septuagint includes Kainan as an extra generation. This is a lens note for understanding the Greek Old Testament; it does not add him to Genesis. Luke 3:36 keeps Kainan by design, following its manuscript evidence. Luke may have included him on purpose; the two genealogies are allowed to differ.

# John 21 source attribution

SBL Greek New Testament, edited by Michael W. Holmes; copyright 2010 Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software. Supplied Faithlife/SBLGNT text and current LICENSE: [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), without warranties. Source: https://github.com/Faithlife/SBLGNT. John 21 extracted, tokenized and NFC normalized; raw token spelling retained. See data/raw/SBLGNT-About.md and SBLGNT-LICENSE.txt for supplied notices.

Tauber, J. K., ed. (2017), *MorphGNT: SBLGNT Edition*, version 6.12, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.376200. https://github.com/morphgnt/sblgnt. Morphological parsing, normalization and lemmatization: [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). The supplied README links an older SBLGNT EULA for its text; we import surface text independently from Faithlife's supplied current CC BY 4.0 text. John 21 analysis extracted and aligned. The combined master and adapted analysis are distributed under CC BY-SA 3.0, retaining the independent CC BY 4.0 source notices. Derived SQLite contains the same adapted data and carries the same notices. No claim that MorphGNT itself has relicensed its text.

STEPBible.org, Tyndale House Cambridge, Translators Amalgamated Greek New Testament (TAGNT): https://github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). John 21 lexical identifiers, dictionary glosses, morphology, edition support and structured variant fields extracted. Running English/Spanish, sub-meanings and explanatory notes excluded. Sanitization and alignment are modifications; no source text corrections asserted. Upstream requests referring readers to its repository for current data. Edition codes are edition support, not dated manuscript witnesses.

Exact upstream commits and local evidence files are recorded in data/sources.tsv. Supplied downloads were fetched 2026-10-20; this implementation performed no network access. Local license evidence is checked again by the import script. data/raw/manifest.tsv records SHA-256 hashes of supplied inputs. No endorsement by the source creators is implied.

Center for New Testament Restoration (CNTR), Electronic Transcriptions, copyright Alan Bunning, https://github.com/Center-for-New-Testament-Restoration/transcriptions (commit 4e743a41a4b2ca010ece53229cd272aa59b1efe6), [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). John 21 lines of the manuscript transcriptions P66, P109, P122, 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 032 and of the WH and RP edition transcriptions extracted to data/raw/CNTR-John21/; collated against SBLGNT by tools/build_variants.py (markup parsed, spelling normalized for comparison, nomina sacra resolved by first/last letter). data/variants/ is an adaptation and is distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0 with this attribution. KJTR, SR and ST files were fetched but are not used.

SBLGNT apparatus (John), same SBLGNT source and license as above (CC BY 4.0), commit c4d241a9c1c479a55b989ba35a4976c1d0b8052c; John 21 entries attached to variation units as edition comparisons.

Manuscript date estimates in data/witnesses.tsv: Wikipedia contributors, "List of New Testament papyri" (oldid 1366826565) and "List of New Testament uncials" (oldid 1354573610), [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/); the pages attribute the dates to INTF palaeographic estimates. Extracted rows in data/raw/WIKIPEDIA-witness-dates.txt.

## Septuagint cross-reference and intertextuality (added 2026-10-20)
STEPBible.org, Tyndale House Cambridge, Translators Amalgamated Hebrew OT (TAHOT), https://github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data (commit ed476a8ee6e3f7b3a46fc48af6c7dabc02387b1d), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Only Hebrew lemma Strong's numbers and Hebrew lemma forms are used, to count co-occurrence per verse; English glosses, translations and notes are not used.

The Old Testament in Greek According to the Septuagint, ed. Henry Barclay Swete (1887–94, public domain), digitized by the Open Greek and Latin Project (First1KGreek, tlg0527) and converted by Nathan Smith, https://github.com/nathans/lxx-swete (commit 26bad3eb42bba98471d154c954e36a6f30a0279d); data [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Word forms are matched for counts only; data/lxx/links.json stores references, counts and form tallies, not the text. data/lxx/ and data/intertext/ are adaptations distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0 with this attribution. The LXX is used as a cross-reference layer only and is not treated as authoritative.

OpenBible.info Cross References, https://www.openbible.info/labs/cross-references/ (downloaded 2026-10-20; file header dated 2026-10-19), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Flagged borderline: links are community-voted (largely from the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge); only John 21 links whose targets share words with the verse are shown, and vote counts are reported, not used as strength.

Considered and not used: CATSS/CCAT LXX morphology and its derivatives (Eliran Wong LXX-Rahlfs-1935, CC BY-NC-SA; CenterBLC/LXX, which states MIT but derives from CATSS), because of the non-commercial user declaration.

## Genesis 11 (Hebrew numbering; LXX Psalm 80)
`data/psa81.jsonl` adapts the pinned STEPBible TAHOT by STEPBible.org / Tyndale House Cambridge, CC BY 4.0, commit ed476a8ee6e3f7b3a46fc48af6c7dabc02387b1d. Source and license: https://github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data and `data/raw/TAHOT/TAHOT-Job-Sng.txt` header. Changes: select Genesis 11, split Hebrew marks into fields, remove slash segmentation for display, retain segmentation in surface_raw, strip all English glosses and notes, use explicit Hebrew references. Morphology and transliteration remain TAHOT's. No separate OSHB/WLC source was imported.

`data/resources/PSA.81.jsonl` and the reader reproduce Swete Psalm 80 word forms from Nathan Smith's nathans/lxx-swete / Open Greek and Latin First1KGreek, pinned 26bad3eb42bba98471d154c954e36a6f30a0279d; data CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://github.com/nathans/lxx-swete). Adaptation: group forms by verse and attach Hebrew verse co-occurrence metadata. The derived Greek-form layer is CC BY-SA 4.0; attribution and ShareAlike must accompany redistribution. Hebrew TAHOT fields retain CC BY 4.0. These forms are secondary cross-reference evidence, never the Hebrew render base.

OpenBible.info cross-reference data, CC BY 4.0 (https://www.openbible.info/labs/cross-references/), is filtered by Hebrew lexical overlap and always flagged BORDERLINE. See `data/sources.tsv` and the raw manifest for pins. Resource and detector candidates are project-generated adaptations, not semantic conclusions.

OSHB morphhb Psalms: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible contributors, [morphhb](https://github.com/openscriptures/morphhb), commit 3d15126fb1ef74867fc1434be1942e837932691f. Morphology and segmentation CC BY 4.0 (data/raw/OSHB/LICENSE.md); based on public-domain Westminster Leningrad Codex. Morpheme data is an adaptation aligned to TAHOT; source-specific vocalization is preserved.
